source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — $3.928 on Thursday June 25, 2026 (Day 118), down from $3.973 (June 19) and below $4.00 since June 18 — a sixth straight weekly decline as crude slid to pre-war lows. The collapse of the war-risk premium followed surging Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic, the US Treasury/OFAC 60-day Iran oil sanctions waiver (General License X, June 22, valid through Aug 21), and Brent's flip into bearish contango (June 24). Brent settled $73.74 and WTI $70.34 on June 24 — both at/near pre-war levels and down ~40% from the wartime peak. Still ~$0.94/gal above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline (~31% higher; AAA/Finder cite $2.96 on Feb 26). Source variance: AAA's homepage showed $3.928 (June 25). Pump relief from the oil slide lags crude by 2-3 weeks; NPR/AP note higher gas, grocery and flight prices will likely outlast the war. The wartime peak was ~$4.54-4.56/gal (NPR June 17 and CFR's Max Boot cite $4.56; AAA print $4.536 on May 6/21), below AAA's nominal record of $5.016 (June 14, 2022). Trump on June 24 ordered DOJ to probe alleged 'gouging' by oil companies for not cutting pump prices faster. Moody's Analytics (NPR) estimates the war has cost US consumers and taxpayers ~$132 billion so far.
